One source only: complexity, dead-code, metrics.

A built-in detector examined these and no external tool did, so nothing corroborates them. Install a tool covering the concern to get a second opinion.

declarations measured by analyzers, completed by built-in detectors: no analyzer supplies cognitive_complexity for Go, Java, JavaScript, Ruby, so the built-in scanner supplied it for those declarations and the analyzers supplied the rest; the criterion set is complete per declaration, which is what makes the rate comparable to the rubric's.

Nothing examined: documentation, structure, style, testing, types.

These concerns are unmeasured, not clean. Install a tool that covers them, or widen analyzers.depth, to have them reported.

Analyzer children are not network-isolated. 11 external tools ran as local child processes. This agent does not transmit the audited source and opens no socket of its own, but it does not sandbox what it spawns: a third-party analyzer that reaches the network is outside what this run controls or observes. Determinism and no upload are the promise; a kernel air-gap is not.
